hits.comment_text:
It's also really nice from a scaling and recovery POV, it's really really hard to have permanent data destruction.

But yes, the IOPS story sadly is (was?) true – we're waiting for this since 7+ year to become available.

From the paper:

  > We have implemented SeaStore to meet real-world requirements and have fully integrated it into the Ceph mainline.
Hmm, latest Ceph 21.2.0 (the .2 is denotes a stable release series in ceph) code named "Umbrella" allows building ceph-crimson OSDs as alternative to the legacy/bluestore ones; but it's not really fully support just yet, at least not for all relevant workloads. So I'm wondering if I'm overlooking something new/fresh, or if they mean that the basic work has been integrated. Don't get me wrong, that alone is definitively an accomplishment for Ceph's non-trivial code base. But especially important core work like auto-scaling placement groups (splits and merges) and the mClock OSD scheduler still are missing, background scrubbing too [0].

Latest docs still got it marked as tech-preview: https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/crimson/crimson/

[0]: https://ceph.io/en/developers/crimson/
